_about: Bitcoin held in outputs whose public key (or spending script) is already visible on-chain, by output category. Unit: BTC amount (not UTXO count). Secondary aggregate published by a third party with an open-source query; not re-run for this snapshot. No price data.

primary.source: Project Eleven, Bitcoin Risq List metrics endpoint
primary.method: SQL over the public BigQuery Bitcoin ETL dataset: (1) outputs whose script type puts a key in the locking script (P2PK, bare multisig, P2TR); (2) unspent balances of P2PKH/P2WPKH/P2SH/P2WSH addresses that have previously been spent from (key or script revealed).

by_category.label: P2PKH address that has already spent (key revealed)
P2WPKH address that has already spent (key revealed)
P2SH script that has already spent (script revealed)
P2WSH script that has already spent (script revealed)

primary.fields_dropped: the endpoint also returns an exchange-rate field; it was deliberately not copied

denominator.formula: sum over heights 0..snapshot height of 50 BTC >> floor(height/210000) (Bitcoin Core GetBlockSubsidy). Upper bound: includes the unspendable genesis output and any subsidy miners did not claim; real UTXO-set total is slightly smaller.

comparison.source: mempool research, UTXO Set Report (orangesurf, 18 May 2025)
comparison.method: bitcoin-utxo-dump (in3rsha) over a Bitcoin Core chainstate snapshot; script type only, no address-reuse analysis
comparison.unit_note: count = number of UTXOs; value = BTC; percentages of the whole UTXO set
comparison.caveat_from_source: The report says it will be updated to fix false identification of <37 byte scripts as P2MS outputs.

limitations: Both figures are third-party aggregates; neither was recomputed from a node for this snapshot.
The two sources use different snapshots (block 892385 vs the primary snapshot height) and different methods, so they agree only in order of magnitude for the overlapping categories (P2PK, P2TR).
Address-reuse categories for P2SH/P2WSH count any previously spent script as exposed even if the revealed script holds no ECDSA/Schnorr key.
Keys exposed off-chain (signed messages, xpub sharing) and in-mempool exposure are not counted.
Shares are computed against scheduled issuance, an upper bound on circulating supply.
